title.zh: 卷472 列傳二百五十九 陆润庠 世续 伊克坦 梁鼎芬 徐坊 劳乃宣 沈曾植
title.en: Volume 472 Biographies 259: Lu Runxiang, Shi Xu, Yi Ketan, Liang Dingfen, Xu Fang, Lao Naixuan, Shen Cengzhi
title.raw: 卷472 列傳二百五十九 陆润庠 世续 伊克坦 梁鼎芬 徐坊 劳乃宣 沈曾植

sentences.zh: 陸潤庠，字鳳石，江蘇元和人。

translations.literal: Lu Runxiang, courtesy name Fengshi, was a native of Yuanhe district in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Runxiang, whose courtesy name was Fengshi, came from Yuanhe in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父懋修，精醫，見藝術傳。

translations.literal: His father Maoxiu was skilled in medicine; see the Biography of Arts and Techniques.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maoxiu was an accomplished physician; he is treated in the Biography of Arts and Techniques.

sentences.zh: 潤庠，同治十三年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: Runxiang, in the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, placed first in the first class of metropolitan graduates and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Tongzhi reign, Runxiang took first place in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，屢典試事，湖南、陝西皆再至。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu he repeatedly served as chief examiner; he went twice each to Hunan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu years he was repeatedly appointed chief examiner, serving twice each in Hunan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 入直南書房，洊擢侍讀。

translations.literal: He entered service in the Southern Library and was promoted in due course to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to the Southern Library and in time was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 出督山東學政。

translations.literal: He was sent out as educational commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as educational commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，再遷祭酒，典試江西。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning period ended, he was again promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and served as chief examiner in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his father, he was again made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and presided over the examinations in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以母疾乞養歸。

translations.literal: On account of his mother's illness he requested leave to nurse her and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he asked leave to care for her and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，起補祭酒，擢內閣學士，署工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled to fill the post of Chancellor, promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and served concurrently as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled as Chancellor, promoted to Grand Secretariat academician, and acted as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西巡，奔赴行在，授禮部侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor toured westward, he rushed to the imperial retinue, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and served as lecturer at the classics lecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor fled west, he hurried to join the court in exile, was named Vice Minister of Rites, and became a lecturer at the imperial classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史，管理醫局，典順天鄉試，充會試副總裁，署工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, managed the Medical Bureau, presided over the Shuntian provincial examination, served as associate chief examiner for the palace examination, and acted as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Left Censor-in-Chief, put in charge of the Medical Bureau, presided over the Shuntian provincial exams, served as deputy chief examiner for the metropolitan finals, and acted as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，充釐訂官制大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he served as a minister charged with revising the official system.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was appointed to the commission revising the official system.

sentences.zh: 已而工部裁省，以尚書兼領順天府尹事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Ministry of Works was abolished, and as Minister he concurrently oversaw affairs as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the Ministry of Works was cut, and he retained his ministerial rank while also taking charge of the Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，授吏部尚書、參預政務大臣，謂：「捐例開，仕途雜，膺民社者或不通曉文義，因訂道府以下考試章程，試不及格者停其分發，設仕學館教習之。」

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of Personnel and Minister with responsibility for government affairs, saying: "With purchase offices opened, the official path has grown mixed, and some who bear responsibility for the people do not understand written norms; therefore examination regulations were drawn up for prefects and below—those who fail the test are barred from assignment, and an Official Learning Hall was established to instruct them."
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Minister of Personnel and a minister with responsibility for government affairs, saying: "With the sale of offices, the civil service had become a jumble and some appointees who governed the people scarcely knew written norms; he therefore set examination rules for officials from prefect downward, barred assignment to those who failed, and founded an Official Learning Hall to train them."

sentences.zh: 潤庠為陸贄後，嘗奏進文集，參以時事，大意謂：「成規未可墨守，而新法亦須斟酌行之。

translations.literal: Runxiang was a descendant of Lu Zhi and once memorialized presenting his collected writings, relating them to current affairs; the gist was: "Established rules cannot be followed slavishly, yet new measures must also be applied with careful judgment.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of the Tang statesman Lu Zhi, Runxiang once submitted his collected writings to the throne, applying them to current affairs. His main point was: "Old regulations must not be followed blindly, but new policies also had to be carried out with careful judgment.

sentences.zh: 若不研求國內歷史，以為變通，必至窒礙難行，且有變本加厲之害。」

translations.literal: If one does not study the nation's own history as a basis for adaptation, measures will inevitably become obstructed and hard to implement, and there will even be harm that grows worse in degree."
translations.idiomatic: Unless one studies the country's own history as a guide to change, reforms will only meet obstruction and may even do harm that grows worse over time."

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，協辦大學士，由體仁閣轉東閣大學士，充弼德院院長。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he served as Associate Grand Secretary, transferred from the Hall of Literary Brilliance to the Eastern Pavilion as Grand Secretary, and became president of the Bide Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong he was made Associate Grand Secretary, moved from the Hall of Literary Brilliance to the Eastern Pavilion, and was appointed president of the Bide Academy.

sentences.zh: 皇帝典學，充毓慶宮授讀，兼顧問大臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor began his classical studies, he served as tutor in the Yuqing Palace and also as advisory minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor undertook his formal studies, he became tutor in the Yuqing Palace and also served as an advisory minister.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「曲阜篤生聖人之地，今新建曲阜學堂，必須闡明經術，提倡正學。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "Qufu is the place where the Sage was born in earnest; now that a Qufu Academy is newly built, the classics must be expounded and orthodox learning promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Qufu is the land where the Sage had truly been born, and the new Qufu Academy must expound the classics and uphold orthodox learning.

sentences.zh: 若雜聘外人，異言異服，喧賓奪主，將來聖教澌滅，亦朝廷之憂。」

translations.literal: If foreigners are hired indiscriminately, with alien speech and dress, the guest will overpower the host, and in time the Sage's teaching will be extinguished—a matter that should also concern the court."
translations.idiomatic: If foreigners were hired indiscriminately, with alien speech and dress, guests would displace the host, and in time the Sage's teaching would fade—a danger the court itself should fear."

sentences.zh: 又陳：「釐訂官制，宜保存臺諫一職。

translations.literal: He also stated: "In revising the official system, the office of censor and remonstrator should be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "In revising the official system, the censorial and remonstrance offices should be kept.

sentences.zh: 說者謂既有國會，不須復有言官。

translations.literal: Some say that once there is a national assembly, remonstrating officials are no longer needed.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that once a parliament existed, there was no need for remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 豈知議員職在立法，言官職在擊邪。

translations.literal: How could they know that the duty of assembly members is legislation, while the duty of remonstrators is to strike down evil?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the duty of parliamentarians is to legislate, while that of remonstrators is to attack wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 議院開會，不過三月，臺諫則隨時可以陳言。

translations.literal: Parliament meets for no more than three months, whereas the censorate and remonstrance bureau may speak at any time.
translations.idiomatic: Parliament sat for only three months, but censors and remonstrators could speak at any time.

sentences.zh: 行政裁判，系定斷於事後，言官則舉發於事前。

translations.literal: Administrative adjudication fixes judgment after the fact; remonstrators expose matters beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative courts ruled only after the fact, whereas remonstrators exposed abuses beforehand.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲開通耳目，則諫院不可裁；

translations.literal: If the court wishes to keep its ears and eyes open, the remonstrance bureau cannot be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: If the court wished to keep its ears open, the remonstrance bureau could not be abolished;

sentences.zh: 諸臣欲鞏固君權，則亦不可言裁。

translations.literal: if ministers wish to consolidate imperial authority, they likewise must not speak of abolishing it.
translations.idiomatic: and if ministers wished to strengthen the sovereign's power, they likewise must not propose abolishing it.

sentences.zh: 即使他時國會成立，亦宜使該院獨立，勿為邪說所淆。」

translations.literal: Even when a national assembly is established in future, that bureau should remain independent and not be confused by heterodox doctrines."
translations.idiomatic: Even when a national assembly was eventually established, that bureau should remain independent and not be swept away by heterodox opinion."

sentences.zh: 又言：「遊學諸生，於實業等事學成而歸者，寥寥可數，而又用非所學。

translations.literal: He also said: "Of students who study abroad, those who complete training in practical industries and the like and return are few in number, and even they are not employed in what they studied.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned: "Of students sent abroad, only a handful returned having mastered practical fields such as industry, and even they were not employed in what they had learned.

sentences.zh: 其最多者惟法政一科。

translations.literal: The largest number study only law and government.
translations.idiomatic: The great majority studied only law and government.

sentences.zh: 法政各國歧異，悉就其本國人情風俗以為製。

translations.literal: Law and government differ in every country; each is fashioned entirely according to its own customs and popular habits.
translations.idiomatic: Law and government differ from country to country; each nation shapes its system to its own customs and habits.

sentences.zh: 今諸生根柢未深，於前古聖賢經傳曾未誦習，道德風尚概未聞知，襲人皮毛，妄言改革；

translations.literal: Today these students' roots are not deep; they have never recited the classics of the ancient sages, know nothing of moral standards and customs, pick up others' surface scraps, and rashly speak of reform;
translations.idiomatic: These students' roots were shallow: they had never studied the classics of the ancient sages, knew nothing of moral culture, picked up foreign surface learning, and rashly preached reform;

sentences.zh: 甚且包藏禍心，倡民權革命之說，判國家與君主為兩途，布其黨徒，潛為謀主。

translations.literal: some even harbor evil intent, advocate popular rights and revolution, treat state and sovereign as two separate paths, spread their partisans, and secretly serve as plotters.
translations.idiomatic: some even harbored treacherous designs, preached popular rights and revolution, separated the state from the sovereign, spread their factions, and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 各部院大臣以為朝廷銳意變法，非重用學生不足以稱上旨，遂乃邪說诐行，遍播中外，久之必致根本動搖，民生塗炭。」

translations.literal: Ministers of the boards and courts, thinking the court was keen on reform and that only by heavily employing students could they satisfy the imperial intent, thus allowed heterodox doctrines and crooked conduct to spread throughout the realm; in time this would surely shake the foundations and bring the people to misery."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, believing the court was bent on reform and that only by favoring returned students could they please the throne, let heterodox and crooked doctrines spread at home and abroad until, in time, the foundations would shake and the people would suffer."

sentences.zh: 又疏陳財用枯竭，請酌停新政，謂：「今日之害，先由於督撫無權，漸而至於朝廷無權。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that finances were exhausted and requested a measured halt to new policies, saying: "Today's harm begins with governors-general and governors lacking authority and gradually extends until the court itself lacks authority.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that the treasury was drained and asked that new policies be scaled back, arguing: "The present harm began with governors losing power and gradually extended until the court itself had none.

sentences.zh: 庫儲之困難，寇賊之充斥，猶其顯而易見者也。

translations.literal: The difficulty of the treasury and the prevalence of bandits are still the most obvious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Empty coffers and rampant banditry were only the most visible signs.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵之設也，所用皆未經歷練之學生，韜略則紙上空談，作用則徒取形式，甚至持不擊同胞之謬說。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of territorial armies, those employed are all untrained students; strategy exists only as empty talk on paper, and in practice they merely adopt forms, some even holding the absurd doctrine of not striking fellow countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: The new territorial armies employed untrained students whose strategy was paper talk and whose operations were mere form, some even preaching the absurd idea that soldiers must not fire on their own countrymen.

sentences.zh: 一旦有事，督撫非但不能調遣，甚且反戈相向，其不可用明矣。

translations.literal: Once trouble arises, governors cannot only fail to deploy them but may even face troops turning their weapons against them; that they are unusable is clear.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis came, governors could not deploy them and might even face mutiny—it was plain they were useless.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦鎮兵，仍取巡防隊而整理之。

translations.literal: It would be better to halt the territorial armies and instead take the patrol forces and put them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Better to abolish the territorial armies and restore and reorganize the old patrol forces.

sentences.zh: 審判之立也，所授皆未曾聽訟之法官，黑白混淆，是非倒置。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of courts, those appointed are all judges who have never heard cases; right and wrong are confused and inverted.
translations.idiomatic: The new courts appointed judges who had never tried a case, confounding right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 舊時諳練之老吏，督撫不得用之，散遣州縣捕役，以緝盜責之巡警。

translations.literal: Experienced clerks of old could not be used by governors; county runners were dispersed, and catching bandits was entrusted to the police.
translations.idiomatic: Experienced former clerks could no longer be used; county constables were dismissed, and bandit suppression was left to the new police.

sentences.zh: 巡警無能也，且不過省會及通商口岸有巡警，豈能分佈​​鄉閭？

translations.literal: The police are incompetent, and moreover they exist only in provincial capitals and treaty ports—how can they be spread through villages?
translations.idiomatic: The police were inept, and existed only in provincial capitals and treaty ports—how could they reach the countryside?

sentences.zh: 將來必至遍地皆盜，人民無可控訴。

translations.literal: In future bandits will surely fill the land and the people will have no one to whom they can appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandits would overrun the land and the people would have nowhere to seek redress.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦審判，仍以聽斷緝捕歸之州縣。

translations.literal: It would be better to halt the courts and again leave hearing cases and catching bandits to the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Better to abolish the new courts and return trials and arrests to the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 諮議局之設也，所舉皆不諳掌故之議員，逞臆狂談，箝制當道，督撫莫能禁之。

translations.literal: As for the provincial assemblies, those elected are all members ignorant of precedent; they indulge wild talk, constrain those in authority, and governors cannot restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial assemblies elected men ignorant of precedent who indulged reckless talk, hamstrung officials, and could not be restrained even by governors.

sentences.zh: 於是藉籌款之名，魚肉鄉里，竊自治之號，私樹黨援。

translations.literal: Thus under the name of raising funds they prey on their districts, steal the title of self-government, and privately build factional ties.
translations.idiomatic: They preyed on the countryside in the name of fundraising, usurped the banner of self-government, and built private factions.

sentences.zh: 上年資政院開議，竟至戟手漫罵，藐視朝廷。

translations.literal: Last year when the Political Consultative Assembly opened, members even pointed fingers and hurled abuse, showing contempt for the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Political Consultative Assembly met the year before, members had pointed fingers and hurled abuse, showing contempt for the throne.

sentences.zh: 以辯給為通才，以橫議為輿論，蜩螗沸羹，莫可究詰。

translations.literal: Glibness is taken for talent, reckless debate for public opinion; like cicadas and boiling soup, nothing can be fully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Eloquence passed for talent and reckless talk for public opinion; the uproar was like boiling soup, beyond any reckoning.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦國會，仍以言事責之諫院。

translations.literal: It would be better to halt the national assembly and again charge the remonstrance bureau with speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Better to suspend parliament and again entrust remonstrance to the censorial bureau.

sentences.zh: 學堂之設也，所聘皆未通經史之教員，其沿用教科書，僅足啟發顓蒙，廢五經而不讀，禍直等於秦焚。

translations.literal: As for the schools, those hired are all teachers ignorant of the classics and histories; the textbooks they use can only enlighten the simple-minded; abandoning the Five Classics without reading them is a calamity equal to the Qin burning of books.
translations.idiomatic: The new schools hired teachers ignorant of the classics; their textbooks could barely instruct beginners; to abandon the Five Classics unread was a disaster equal to the Qin book-burning.

sentences.zh: 暑假、星期，毫無拘束，彼血氣未定者，豈不結黨為非？

translations.literal: Summer vacation and weekly holidays impose no restraint at all; will not those whose blood and vigor are unsettled form factions and do wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Summer vacation and weekly holidays left students wholly unrestrained; would hot-blooded youths not form factions and make trouble?

sentences.zh: 又膳學費百倍於前，致使貧寒聰穎之士流，進身無路。

translations.literal: Moreover board and tuition are a hundred times what they were before, so that poor but clever scholars have no path to advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Board and tuition cost a hundred times more than before, shutting poor but gifted scholars out of advancement.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦中小學堂，仍用經策取士。

translations.literal: It would be better to halt primary and secondary schools and again select officials by classical examination.
translations.idiomatic: Better to close the primary and secondary schools and again select officials by classical examination.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆於財政有關，而禍不僅在財政，使不早為之所，必至權柄下移，大局不可收拾。」

translations.literal: All these relate to finance, yet the harm is not only financial; if measures are not taken early, authority will surely shift downward and the overall situation will become unmanageable."
translations.idiomatic: All these bore on finance, yet the harm was not financial alone; unless checked early, power would drain downward and the realm would slip beyond control."

sentences.zh: 疏上，多不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, most of it received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Most of these memorials went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 時建設立憲內閣，宰輔擁虛名而已。

translations.literal: At the time a constitutional cabinet was being formed, and chief ministers held only empty titles.
translations.idiomatic: A constitutional cabinet was then being formed, but the chief ministers held only empty titles.

sentences.zh: 武昌兵變，官軍既克漢陽，武昌旦夕下。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang mutiny broke out, government troops had already taken Hanyang and Wuchang would fall within days.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wuchang mutiny, imperial troops took Hanyang and Wuchang seemed about to fall.

sentences.zh: 而新內閣又成立，總理大臣袁世凱議修和息戰禍，取隆裕太后懿旨，頒示天下，改建國體，於是遜位詔下矣。

translations.literal: Then a new cabinet was formed; Prime Minister Yuan Shikai proposed peace to end the calamity of war, obtained an edict from Empress Dowager Longyu, and promulgated it throughout the realm to change the form of state—and thus the abdication edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: A new cabinet was formed; Prime Minister Yuan Shikai sought peace to end the war, secured an edict from Empress Dowager Longyu, and proclaimed a change of polity to the empire—and so the abdication decree came down.

sentences.zh: 潤庠以老瞶辭授讀差，奉懿旨仍照料毓慶宮，給月俸如故，授太保。

translations.literal: Runxiang, citing age and dim sight, resigned his tutoring post; by imperial edict he was still to oversee the Yuqing Palace, his monthly salary continued as before, and he was appointed Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Runxiang resigned his tutoring post on grounds of age and failing sight; by edict he was still to oversee the Yuqing Palace at his former salary and was made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 越二年，病卒，年七十五，贈太傅，諡文端。

translations.literal: Two years later he died of illness, aged seventy-five; he was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died of illness at seventy-five; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 潤庠性和易，接物無崖岸，雖貴，服用如為諸生時。

translations.literal: Runxiang's nature was easygoing; in dealing with others he had no lofty barrier; though honored, his dress and use were as when he was a student.
translations.idiomatic: Runxiang was easygoing and unpretentious in company; even in high rank he dressed and lived as he had as a student.

sentences.zh: 遇變憂鬱，內結於胸而外不露。

translations.literal: When crisis came he was melancholy, knotting grief within his breast while showing nothing outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: When upheaval came he grew melancholy, brooding inwardly while showing nothing outwardly.

sentences.zh: 及病篤，竟日危坐，瞑目不言，亦不食，數日而逝。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, he sat upright all day with eyes closed and spoke not, nor ate, and died after several days.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned grave he sat upright all day with closed eyes, neither speaking nor eating, and died after several days.

sentences.zh: 世續，字伯軒，索勒豁金氏，隸內務府滿洲正黃旗。

translations.literal: Shi Xu, courtesy name Boxuan, of the Suoluhojin clan, was registered with the Internal Affairs Office in the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xu, whose courtesy name was Boxuan, belonged to the Suoluhojin clan and was registered with the Internal Affairs Office in the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年舉人，以議敘主事歷內務府郎中，擢武備院卿，授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination as juren; by merit he rose from clerk to director in the Internal Affairs Office, was promoted to Director of the Armory, and appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of Guangxu, rose through the Internal Affairs Office from clerk to director, was promoted to Director of the Armory, and became a Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，為總管內務府大臣，兼工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he became Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office and concurrently Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office and concurrently Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，各國聯軍入京，兩宮西狩，適遭父喪，命留京辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the allied armies of various nations entered Beijing and the two empress dowagers fled west, he happened to be mourning his father and was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the allied powers entered Beijing and the Empress Dowager and the Emperor fled west, he was mourning his father and was ordered to stay in the capital to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 即日縗墨詣聯軍請保護宮廷​​，日為宮中備飲饌，並保壇廟。

translations.literal: That very day, wearing mourning garb, he went to the allied forces to request protection for the palace, daily provisioned food and drink for the court, and protected the altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, still in mourning dress, he went to the allied commanders to seek protection for the palace, supplied the court with food daily, and guarded the altars and temples.

sentences.zh: 晉理籓院尚書，調禮部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 兩宮回鑾，賞黃馬褂，轉吏部，兼都統。

translations.literal: When the two empress dowagers returned, he was awarded the yellow riding jacket, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and served concurrently as banner general.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor returned, he was given the yellow riding jacket, moved to the Ministry of Personnel, and also served as banner general.

sentences.zh: 內務府三旗甲米向歸吏胥代領折價，名曰「米折」，所得甚微。

translations.literal: The grain stipends for the three banners under the Internal Affairs Office had long been collected for them by clerks at discounted rates under the name "rice conversion," yielding very little.
translations.idiomatic: Grain stipends for the three Internal Affairs banners had long been collected by clerks at cut rates under the name "rice conversion," leaving the recipients very little.

sentences.zh: 世續商之倉場，飭旗丁自領，眾感實惠。

translations.literal: Shi Xu negotiated with the granary office and ordered banner soldiers to collect in person; the people were grateful for the real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xu arranged with the granary that banner soldiers collect their grain in person, to everyone's real benefit.

sentences.zh: 纂呈四書圖說，特旨褒嘉。

translations.literal: He compiled and presented Illustrated Explanations of the Four Books and received special imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled and presented Illustrated Explanations of the Four Books and received special imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，尋授體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, as Minister of Personnel he was made Associate Grand Secretary, and soon received appointment as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, as Minister of Personnel he became Associate Grand Secretary and soon Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 歷轉文華殿大學士，充憲政編查館參預政務大臣。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and served as Minister with responsibility for government affairs under the Constitutional Research Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and served as a minister with responsibility for government affairs on the Constitutional Research Commission.

sentences.zh: 念八旗生計日艱，奏設工藝廠，俾習工藝贍身家。

translations.literal: Concerned that banner livelihoods were growing daily more strained, he memorialized to establish craft workshops so they could learn trades to support their families.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing banner livelihoods grow harder by the day, he memorialized to open craft workshops so bannermen could learn trades to support their families.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，議繼體，世續獨言國事艱危，宜立長君，不能用。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong died and succession was debated, Shi Xu alone argued that with the state in peril an elder ruler should be installed; his view was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangxu died and succession was debated, Shi Xu alone urged that in such peril an older ruler should be chosen; his advice was rejected.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，以疾乞休。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Xuantong, he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年，復起原官，仍兼總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled to his former post and still concurrently served as Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to his former posts and again served as Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office.

sentences.zh: 及議遜位，世續首讚之。

translations.literal: When abdication was discussed, Shi Xu was first to endorse it.
translations.idiomatic: When abdication was discussed, Shi Xu was the first to endorse it.

sentences.zh: 太后令磋商優待條件，授太保。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered negotiation of favorable treatment terms and appointed him Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered negotiations on favorable terms for the abdication and appointed him Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 接修崇陵工程，加太傅。

translations.literal: He took charge of repairing the Chongling Mausoleum project and was promoted to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He took charge of repairs to the Chongling Mausoleum and was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 丁巳復辟，懼禍及，力阻之。

translations.literal: At the 1917 restoration he feared disaster would reach him and strenuously opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: During the 1917 restoration he feared he would be implicated and strongly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 事變亟，入宿衛，並以殮服自隨。

translations.literal: When events turned urgent, he entered to stand night guard and brought burial garments with him.
translations.idiomatic: When events turned urgent he entered the palace as night guard and carried burial garments with him.

sentences.zh: 頻年以經費拮据，支持尤苦，纂修德宗實錄，始終其事，及書成，已病不能起矣。

translations.literal: Year after year with funds tight, support was especially hard; he edited the Veritable Records of Dezong from start to finish, and when the book was finished he was already too ill to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Funds were tight year after year and the burden was especially heavy; he saw the Veritable Records of Guangxu through from start to finish, and when the work was done he was too ill to rise.

sentences.zh: 辛酉年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the xinyou year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the xinyou year, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，諡文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 伊克坦，字仲平，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人，西安駐防。

translations.literal: Yi Ketan, courtesy name Zhongping, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner stationed at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketan, whose courtesy name was Zhongping, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan; he was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner garrisoned at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年進士，以編修歷至都察院副都​​御史，充滿蒙文學堂監督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he passed as jinshi; from compiler he rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and served as superintendent of the Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Guangxu, rose from Hanlin compiler to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as superintendent of the Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy.

sentences.zh: 有請達海從祀文廟者，伊克坦以達海創定國書，繙譯經史，有功聖教，允宜附祀，即為代奏，略言：「學官立於漢京，而配享實始於唐代，宋、元以來，迭有增祀，大率以闡明聖學，有功經訓為斷。

translations.literal: When someone requested that Dahai be granted collateral sacrifice in the Confucian temple, Yi Ketan held that Dahai had created and fixed the national script and translated the classics and histories, meriting service to the Sage's teaching, and that collateral sacrifice was proper; he memorialized on his behalf, stating in brief: "School officials were established in the Han capital, but collateral sacrifice in the temple actually began in the Tang; since Song and Yuan there have been repeated additions, generally judged by whether one expounded the Sage's learning and served the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When a petition asked that Dahai be enshrined in the Confucian temple, Yi Ketan argued that Dahai had devised the national script and translated the classics, thus serving the Sage's teaching, and deserved collateral sacrifice; he memorialized on his behalf, noting briefly: "School officials dated to Han times but temple collateral sacrifice began in the Tang, and since Song and Yuan additions had generally honored those who expounded the Sage's learning and served the classics.

sentences.zh: 漢儒許慎，特因說文解字，功在經籍，專隆升祔。

translations.literal: The Han scholar Xu Shen was specially elevated to collateral sacrifice solely because Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters served the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Han scholar Xu Shen had been specially elevated solely because his Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters served the study of the classics.

sentences.zh: 我太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝指授文臣創立國書，傳譯經史，宣布文教，尤極千古未有之盛。

translations.literal: Our Taizu, the High Emperor, and Taizong, the Literary Emperor, directed civil officials to create the national script, transmit and translate the classics and histories, and proclaim civil culture—a splendor unmatched in all ages.
translations.idiomatic: Our Taizu and Taizong had directed civil officials to create the national script, translate the classics and histories, and spread civil culture—a splendor without parallel in history.

sentences.zh: 夫國書字體，創自文臣額爾德尼及噶蓋等，而仰承聖意，匯集大成，詳定頒行者，實唯儒臣達海。

translations.literal: As for the forms of the national script, they were first created by the civil officials Erdeni and Gagai and others, but it was the Confucian official Dahai alone who, following the imperial intent, gathered the great synthesis, fixed it in detail, and promulgated it.
translations.idiomatic: The script itself had been devised by Erdeni, Gagai, and others, but it was the Confucian official Dahai who, following the imperial will, brought the system together, refined it, and promulgated it.

sentences.zh: 達海以肇造貞元之佐，擅閎通著述之才，歷相兩朝，瞻言百里。

translations.literal: Dahai, as an assistant at the founding of the dynasty's true origin, excelled in broad learning and literary talent, served as chief minister through two reigns, and his words were heeded for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai had been a founding assistant of the dynasty, possessed broad literary talent, served as chief minister under two emperors, and his counsel carried great weight.

sentences.zh: 其初奉命詳定國書，重加圈點，發明音義；

translations.literal: At first he was ordered to fix the national script in detail, add dots anew, and clarify pronunciation and meaning;
translations.idiomatic: At first he was ordered to refine the national script, add punctuation, and clarify pronunciation and meaning;

sentences.zh: 又以國書漢字對音未全，於十二字頭之外有所增加，而國書之用乃廣。

translations.literal: because the phonetic correspondence between the national script and Chinese characters was incomplete, he made additions beyond the twelve syllabaries, and thus the use of the national script broadened.
translations.idiomatic: because phonetic correspondence between Manchu and Chinese was incomplete, he added characters beyond the twelve syllabaries, greatly extending the script's use.

sentences.zh: 复定兩字切音之法，較之漢文切音，更為精當，而國書之制乃備。

translations.literal: He further fixed the method of two-character phonetic spelling, which compared with Chinese fanqie is more precise and exact, and thus the system of the national script was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised a two-character spelling method more precise than Chinese fanqie, completing the national script as a system.

sentences.zh: 繙譯經典，昭示群倫，功不在傳經諸儒下。

translations.literal: He translated the classics and made them clear to all ranks; his merit is not below the Confucian scholars who transmitted the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In translating the classics and bringing them before all the world, his achievement was no less than that of the scholars who had handed the classics down.

sentences.zh: 崇德十年，既蒙賜諡文成，康熙九年，复奉賜文立碑，隆德報功，永受恩澤。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongde he received the posthumous title Wencheng; in the ninth year of Kangxi he was again granted a stele inscribed with the character wen—honoring virtue and repaying merit, he received imperial grace forever.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chongde he was granted the posthumous title Wencheng; in the ninth year of Kangxi a stele bearing the character wen was erected in his honor—virtue exalted, merit rewarded, his name forever under imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 旋有學士阿理瑚奏請從祀文廟，禮臣復奏，以為創造國書，一藝之長，不當從祀，未經議準。

translations.literal: Soon Academician Arihu memorialized requesting collateral sacrifice in the Confucian temple; the ritual officials memorialized again, holding that creating the national script was mastery of a single art and unworthy of collateral sacrifice—it was not approved by deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Academician Arihu petitioned for Dahai's enshrinement in the Confucian temple; the Board of Rites replied that devising the national script was excellence in but one art and did not warrant collateral sacrifice, and the request was never approved.

sentences.zh: 查達海詳定國書字體，實禀太宗指示而成。

translations.literal: Investigation shows that Dahai's detailed fixing of the national script forms was in fact completed by following Taizong's instructions.
translations.idiomatic: On inquiry, Dahai's refinement of the national script had in truth been carried out under Taizong's direction.

sentences.zh: 作者為聖，述者為明，非唯羽翼六經，抑且昭示百世。

translations.literal: The author is the Sage; the expounder is the illuminator—it not only wings the Six Classics but also makes them clear for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Sage writes; the expositor illuminates—not only did he give wings to the Six Classics, he made their light shine for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 部議謂僅一藝之長，實未深知大體。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberation held that it was merely mastery of one art and truly failed to grasp the larger principle.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry's ruling—that this was only a single craft—showed a failure to grasp the larger matter.

sentences.zh: 達海於聖經有表章之力，於後學有津逮之功。

translations.literal: Dahai had the power to elucidate the sacred classics and the merit of providing a ford for later students.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai had elucidated the sacred classics and opened a path for generations of students who came after.

sentences.zh: 方今宗學、旗學兼重國書，並奉旨特設滿蒙文學堂於京師，奉省亦經奏立八旗滿蒙文中學堂。

translations.literal: At present the imperial clan schools and banner schools alike stress the national script; by imperial order a Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy was specially established in the capital, and Fengtian province also memorialized to establish Eight Banner Manchu-Mongol middle schools.
translations.idiomatic: Today the imperial clan schools and banner schools alike give weight to the national script; by imperial command a Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy was specially set up in the capital, and Fengtian province has likewise memorialized to establish Eight Banner Manchu-Mongol middle schools.

sentences.zh: 揆諸古者釋奠祭師之誼，達海應得附祀，核與漢儒許慎從祀之例亦屬相符。

translations.literal: Measured against the ancient meaning of the libation sacrifice honoring teachers, Dahai ought to receive collateral sacrifice; checked against the precedent of the Han scholar Xu Shen's collateral sacrifice, it is also conformable.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by the ancient rite of the libation sacrifice honoring teachers, Dahai deserves collateral sacrifice; compared with the precedent of the Han scholar Xu Shen, the case is entirely in accord.

sentences.zh: 仰懇俯準達海附祀文廟，並請敕建專祠於盛京，以昭矜式。

translations.literal: Humbly begging approval for Dahai's collateral sacrifice in the Confucian temple, and requesting an order to build a dedicated shrine at Mukden, to display a model for admiration.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Dahai be granted collateral sacrifice in the Confucian temple, and that an order be issued to erect a dedicated shrine at Mukden, that all may have a model to revere.

sentences.zh: 查盛京東門外尚有達海塋墓，榛莽荒蕪，碣碑剝落，並請敕下所司修治看護，用示朝廷崇尚實學、藎念儒臣之至意。」

translations.literal: Investigation shows that east of Mukden's outer gate there is still Dahai's tomb, overgrown with thorns and weeds, its stele crumbling; also requesting an order to the relevant offices for repair and upkeep, to show the court's esteem for practical learning and utmost care for Confucian officials."
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry shows that east of Mukden's outer gate Dahai's tomb still stands, choked with weeds, its stele flaking away; I also beg that the responsible offices be ordered to repair and guard it, that the court's esteem for practical learning and its deep regard for Confucian ministers may be made plain."

sentences.zh: 又代陳典學事宜，略言：「伏讀雍正三年世宗憲皇帝諭：'帝王禦宇膺圖，咸資典學。'

translations.literal: He also memorialized on matters of classical learning on another's behalf, stating in brief: "Having read reverently the edict of the Xian Emperor Shizong in the third year of Yongzheng: 'When emperors hold the realm and receive the mandate, all rely on classical learning.'
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial on classical learning on another's behalf, stating in brief: "I have read with reverence the edict of the Xian Emperor Shizong in the third year of Yongzheng: 'When an emperor takes the realm and receives the mandate, he must rely on classical learning.'

sentences.zh: 我聖祖仁皇帝天亶聰明，而好古敏求，六十餘年孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Our Sage Ancestor the Benevolent Emperor was heaven-endowed with intelligence, yet loved antiquity and pursued learning keenly, for more than sixty years never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Our Sage Ancestor the Benevolent Emperor was gifted with heaven's intelligence, yet loved antiquity and sought learning with keen diligence—for more than sixty years he never flagged.

sentences.zh: 又喜慶二十四年仁宗睿皇帝：'帝王之學，在於貫徹天人，明體達用，以見諸施行，與經生尋章索句者不同。'

translations.literal: And in the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, the Sage Emperor Renzong said: 'The emperor's learning lies in penetrating Heaven and man, clarifying principle and achieving practical use, making it visible in conduct—different from classicists who hunt passages and seek phrases.'
translations.idiomatic: And in the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, the Sage Emperor Renzong said: 'The emperor's learning must unite Heaven and man, grasp principle and put it to use, and be seen in what is actually done—it is not the same as scholars who hunt through chapters for isolated lines.'

sentences.zh: 仰見列聖相承，重視典學之至意。

translations.literal: One sees reverently how successive sages inherited one another's utmost intent to value classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one sees, with reverence, how successive sage emperors handed down their deepest intent to honor classical learning.

sentences.zh: 我皇上睿哲性成，聰明天縱，衝齡踐祚，洪業肇基，當此春秋典學之時，實為聖敬日躋之始，伏維監國攝政王薰陶德性，輔養聖躬，慎選侍從，左右將護，亦既淵衝翕受，法戒靡遺。

translations.literal: Our Emperor is by nature wise and sagacious, heaven-talented and bright; ascending the throne at a tender age, with the great enterprise newly begun, at this time of spring years and classical learning it is truly the beginning of daily advance in sagely reverence; I consider that the regent prince overseeing the realm has nurtured his moral nature, assisted in raising the imperial person, carefully chosen attendants, and guarded him on every side—already the deep child has received it all, and no lesson or warning has been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Our Emperor is wise and sagacious by nature, bright with heaven's gift; he ascended the throne in tender years, the great enterprise only just begun. At this season of youth and classical study, it is truly the beginning of daily ascent in sagely reverence. The regent prince overseeing the realm has shaped his moral nature, nurtured the imperial person, chosen attendants with care, and guarded him on every side—the young emperor has already absorbed it all, and no lesson or warning has been spared.

sentences.zh: 唯是皇上一念之張弛，系萬機之治忽；

translations.literal: Only the emperor's single thought of looseness or tautness ties to the rise or neglect of the myriad affairs of state;
translations.idiomatic: Yet a single moment's slackening or tightening in the emperor's mind bears upon whether the myriad affairs of state flourish or fail;

sentences.zh: 一朝之規制，系薄海之觀瞻。

translations.literal: a court's institutions tie to the gaze of all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: a court's institutions bear upon how all beneath the seas regard the throne.

sentences.zh: 有不得不慎之又慎者，謹為我皇上詳晰陳之：一，請崇聖學。

translations.literal: There are matters where one cannot but be ever more cautious; respectfully for Our Emperor I state them in detail: First, please exalt sagely learning.
translations.idiomatic: Some things must be guarded with redoubled care; I respectfully set them out in detail for Our Emperor: First, I ask that sagely learning be exalted.

sentences.zh: 易端蒙養，禮重師教，書述遜敏，詩頌緝熙，聖學精微，非尋常科學範圍之所能及。

translations.literal: The Changes begins with early nurture, the Rites honors the teacher's instruction, the Documents describes humility and quickness, the Odes praises bright harmony—sagely learning is subtle and fine, beyond what ordinary branches of learning can reach.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes begins with early nurture, the Rites honors the teacher's instruction, the Documents speaks of humility and quickness, the Odes praises bright harmony—sagely learning is subtle and profound, beyond the reach of ordinary branches of study.

sentences.zh: 宋儒有言'帝王之學，與儒生異尚'，與我仁宗睿皇帝典學之諭用意正符。

translations.literal: Song scholars said, 'The emperor's learning differs in aim from that of the Confucian scholar,' which matches exactly the intent of Our Sage Emperor Renzong's edict on classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Song scholars said that 'the emperor's learning pursues a different end from that of the Confucian scholar'—words that match exactly the intent of Our Sage Emperor Renzong's edict on classical learning.

sentences.zh: 今我皇上典學之初，應定教學科目，自應會通今古，融貫中西，不可拘於舊例。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of Our Emperor's classical studies, the subjects of instruction ought to be fixed; they should naturally unite past and present and integrate Chinese and Western learning, and must not be bound by old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Now, at the outset of Our Emperor's classical studies, the curriculum ought to be set: it should unite past and present and draw together Chinese and Western learning, and not be confined to old precedent.

sentences.zh: 伏乞簡派儒臣，詳細籌訂，鑑成憲，酌時宜，毋徒陳進講之空文，毋虛循延英之故事，庶足以開張聖聽，裨益亶聰，以立聖學聖治之基。

translations.literal: Humbly begging that Confucian officials be selected and dispatched to plan in detail, taking past statutes as mirror and weighing present needs, neither offering empty memorials of lectures submitted nor hollowly following the old story of the Yanying Hall, so that the imperial ear may be opened and heaven-endowed intelligence enriched, laying the foundation for sagely learning and sagely rule.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that learned officials be chosen and sent to draw up the plan in detail, taking established precedent as mirror and present needs as measure—neither submitting empty memorials about lectures nor going through the hollow motions of the old Yanying Hall ritual—so that the imperial ear may be opened, heaven's gift sharpened, and the foundation laid for sagely learning and sagely rule.

sentences.zh: 一，請擇賢傅。

translations.literal: Second, please select worthy tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Second, I ask that worthy tutors be chosen.

sentences.zh: 舊制師傅向以大臣選充，期於老成典型，成就君德，然或入官從政，講學非其所長。

translations.literal: Under the old system tutors were generally chosen from among grand ministers, with the hope that mature exemplars would complete the ruler's virtue; yet some entered office and engaged in politics, and lecturing was not their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system tutors were usually drawn from among grand ministers, in the hope that seasoned exemplars would complete the ruler's virtue; yet some were men of office and politics, for whom lecturing was not their strength.

sentences.zh: 老師大儒，潛德隱而勿耀，而教育精深，尤非研究有素，不能取益。

translations.literal: Old masters and great scholars, their hidden virtue concealed and not displayed, yet profound in teaching—benefit cannot be gained unless one has long studied the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Old masters and great scholars keep their hidden virtue from display, yet their teaching runs deep—only those who have long pursued the subject can truly profit from them.

sentences.zh: 擬請敕下內外大臣，各舉所知，勿拘資格，略仿乾隆十四年詔舉經學人員成例，擇其品端學粹、教育卓著成績者，請旨召用，隆以師傅之任，分門講教，而仍派大臣總司其成，俾專日講於經筵，不必更勞以職事。

translations.literal: It is proposed to request an order to ministers within and without, each to recommend those they know without being bound by qualifications, roughly following the precedent of the fourteenth year of Qianlong's edict summoning specialists in classical learning; choosing those of upright character, pure learning, and outstanding teaching achievement, begging the throne to summon and employ them, elevating them to the post of tutor, assigning them to teach by subject, while still dispatching a grand minister to oversee the whole, so that they may devote themselves daily to the classics lecture without being further burdened with official duties.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that ministers at court and in the provinces be ordered each to recommend men they know, without regard to formal qualifications, following roughly the precedent of Qianlong's fourteenth-year edict summoning specialists in classical learning; those of upright character, pure scholarship, and proven teaching merit should be summoned by imperial command, raised to the rank of tutor, and assigned to teach by subject, while a grand minister is still appointed to oversee the whole, so that they may lecture daily at the classics lecture without being further burdened with official duties.

sentences.zh: 其任彌專，其責彌重，其效彌速，使天下曉然於尊師崇儒之意，庶儒林有所矜式，而聖德日進高明矣。

translations.literal: The more dedicated the post, the heavier the responsibility, the swifter the effect—so that all under Heaven clearly understand the intent to honor teachers and exalt Confucian learning; then the Confucian community will have a model to admire, and sagely virtue will daily advance to greater heights.
translations.idiomatic: The more dedicated the post, the heavier the responsibility, the swifter the result—so that all under Heaven may plainly see the intent to honor teachers and exalt Confucian learning; then the scholarly community will have a model to revere, and sagely virtue will daily rise to greater heights.

sentences.zh: 一，請肅​​規制。

translations.literal: Third, please tighten regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Third, I ask that regulations be tightened.

sentences.zh: 古者聖王教冑，必選端方正直、道術博聞之士，與之居處，是以習與智長，化與心成。

translations.literal: In antiquity when sage kings taught the heir, they always chose men upright and straight, broad in the Way and learned, to dwell with him—thus habit grew with wisdom, and transformation was completed in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when sage kings instructed the heir, they chose men upright and learned in the Way to dwell with him—so that habit grew with wisdom and transformation took root in the heart.

sentences.zh: 我皇上毓德方新，始基宜固，舊制選派內監伴讀，似不足以肅學製而廣箴規。

translations.literal: Our Emperor's moral cultivation is newly begun and the foundation ought to be firm; the old system of selecting eunuchs as reading companions seems insufficient to tighten the school system and broaden admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Our Emperor's moral cultivation has only just begun, and the foundation ought to be made firm; the old practice of assigning eunuchs as reading companions seems insufficient to give the school system proper gravity or to broaden the scope of admonition.

sentences.zh: 擬請改選王公大臣之賢子弟昕夕侍從，斅學相長，並參考學校制度，建設講堂，陳列圖書彝器，觀摩肄習，以收敬業樂群之效。

translations.literal: It is proposed to request instead the selection of worthy sons of princes, dukes, and grand ministers to attend morning and evening, learning from one another; also, with reference to school institutions, to build lecture halls, display books and ritual vessels, and observe and practice together, to achieve the effect of reverent devotion to study and delight in good company.
translations.idiomatic: I propose instead that worthy sons of princes, dukes, and grand ministers be chosen to attend morning and evening, learning from one another; and, drawing on school institutions, that lecture halls be built, books and ritual vessels displayed, and study observed and practiced together, to achieve reverent devotion to learning and delight in good company.

sentences.zh: 以上三事，僅舉大綱。

translations.literal: The three matters above merely set forth the main outline.
translations.idiomatic: These three matters set forth only the main outline.

sentences.zh: 我皇上今日之言動起居，罔有勿敬，即異日之立政敷教，罔有勿臧，此尤根本之至計，不可不謹之於漸，而慎之於始者也。

translations.literal: Our Emperor's words, conduct, and daily life today are without anything un-reverent; likewise his future establishment of policy and spreading of instruction will be without anything un-good—this above all is the root plan, which cannot but be guarded gradually and cautioned at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Our Emperor's words, conduct, and daily life today are without anything irreverent; likewise, when he later establishes policy and spreads instruction, nothing will be amiss—this above all is the root plan, which must be guarded from the first and watched from the very beginning.

sentences.zh: 伏念朝廷廣勵人才，振興教育，侁侁學子，爭自濯磨，皇上典學伊始，益宜宏茲遠謨，以慰天下士民之望。」

translations.literal: Reflecting that the court broadly encourages talent and revives education, and eager students everywhere strive to polish themselves, at the very outset of the emperor's classical studies it is all the more fitting to expand this far-reaching design, to satisfy the hopes of scholars and people throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that the court broadly encourages talent and revives education, and eager students everywhere strive to refine themselves, at the very outset of the emperor's classical studies it is all the more fitting to expand this far-reaching design and satisfy the hopes of scholars and common people throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，伊克坦與大學士陸潤庠及侍郎陳寶琛，同奉命直毓慶宮，朝夕入講，遇事進言，憂勤彌甚。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, Yi Ketan together with Grand Secretary Lu Runxiang and Vice Minister Chen Baochen were alike ordered to serve on duty at the Yuqing Palace, entering daily to lecture, offering remonstrance when matters arose, their worry and diligence ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuantong, Yi Ketan, Grand Secretary Lu Runxiang, and Vice Minister Chen Baochen were alike ordered to serve at the Yuqing Palace; they lectured morning and evening, spoke up when matters arose, and their worry and diligence only grew.

sentences.zh: 丁巳復辟，潤庠已前卒，寶琛為議政大臣，伊克坦一不爭權位，日進講如故。

translations.literal: At the 1917 restoration Runxiang had already died earlier; Baochen was a deliberative minister, and Yi Ketan alone did not contend for power or position, continuing daily lectures as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the 1917 restoration Runxiang had already died; Baochen served as a deliberative minister, and Yi Ketan alone did not contend for power or position, lecturing daily as before.

sentences.zh: 及事變，誓臨危以身殉。

translations.literal: When events turned, he vowed that in peril he would give his life.
translations.idiomatic: When events turned against them, he vowed to give his life if danger came.

sentences.zh: 伊克坦忠直有遠識，主開誠佈公，集思廣益；

translations.literal: Yi Ketan was loyal, upright, and far-sighted, advocating openness and sincerity and gathering many minds for broad benefit;
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketan was loyal, upright, and far-sighted; he favored openness and sincerity and gathering many minds for the common good;

sentences.zh: 而左右慮患深，務趨避，時復相左。

translations.literal: yet those around him feared trouble deeply and strove to avoid it, and at times they opposed one another.
translations.idiomatic: yet those around him feared trouble deeply and sought only to avoid it, and at times they worked against him.

sentences.zh: 伊克坦憂鬱遂久病，日寄於酒。

translations.literal: Yi Ketan, depressed, then fell into long illness and daily took refuge in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketan, worn down by grief, fell into long illness and took refuge in wine day after day.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，卒，年五十有八，諡文直。

translations.literal: In the guihai year he died, aged fifty-eight, posthumous name Wenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the guihai year he died, aged fifty-eight, and was given the posthumous name Wenzhi.

sentences.zh: 梁鼎芬，字星海，廣東番禺人。

translations.literal: Liang Dingfen, courtesy name Xinghai, was a native of Panyu in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dingfen, whose courtesy name was Xinghai, came from Panyu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he passed as jinshi and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 法越事亟，疏劾北洋大臣李鴻章，不報。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese affair grew urgent, he memorialized impeaching Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang; no response was received.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese crisis grew urgent, he memorialized impeaching Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 旋又追論妄劾，交部嚴議，降五級調用。

translations.literal: Soon afterward a counter-charge of reckless impeachment was pursued; the matter was referred to the ministry for strict deliberation, and he was demoted five ranks and reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was pursued on a charge of reckless impeachment; the matter was referred to the ministry for strict deliberation, and he was demoted five ranks and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 張之洞督粵，聘主廣雅書院講席；

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhidong governed Guangdong, he was engaged to head the lecture chair at the Guangya Academy;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong governed Guangdong, he was invited to head the lecture chair at the Guangya Academy;

sentences.zh: 調署兩江，复聘主鍾山書院；

translations.literal: transferred to act in the Two Jiangs, he was again engaged to head the Zhongshan Academy;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang was transferred to act in the Two Jiangs, he was again invited to head the Zhongshan Academy;

sentences.zh: 又隨還鄂，皆參其幕府事。

translations.literal: when Zhang returned to Hubei, he followed and likewise served in his secretariat on all occasions.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang returned to Hubei, Dingfen followed and served in his secretariat throughout.

sentences.zh: 之洞銳行新政，學堂林立，言學事惟鼎芬是任。

translations.literal: Zhidong vigorously pursued the new policies, schools sprang up everywhere, and on matters of education only Dingfen was entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong vigorously pursued the new policies, schools sprang up everywhere, and on all matters of education only Dingfen was entrusted.

sentences.zh: 拳禍起，兩宮西幸，鼎芬首倡呈進方物之議。

translations.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose and the two empress dowagers fled west, Dingfen was first to propose presenting local tribute products.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer calamity broke out and the Empress Dowager and the Emperor fled west, Dingfen was first to propose presenting local tribute products.

sentences.zh: 初以端方薦，起用直隸州知州；

translations.literal: At first, on Duanfang's recommendation, he was recalled as prefect of a Zhili subprefecture;
translations.idiomatic: At first, on Duanfang's recommendation, he was recalled as prefect of a Zhili subprefecture;

sentences.zh: 之洞再薦，詔赴行在所，用知府，發湖北，署武昌，補漢陽。

translations.literal: Zhidong recommended him again; he was ordered to proceed to the imperial retinue, appointed prefect, sent to Hubei, acted as prefect of Wuchang, and was then appointed to Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong recommended him again; he was ordered to the imperial retinue, appointed prefect, sent to Hubei, acted as prefect of Wuchang, and was then appointed to Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 擢安襄鄖荊道、按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit, appointed surveillance commissioner, and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit, made surveillance commissioner, and acted as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 奏請化除滿、漢界限。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting the abolition of Manchu-Han distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that Manchu-Han distinctions be abolished.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，入覲，面劾慶親王奕劻通賕賄，請月給銀三萬兩以養其廉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he attended audience at court and in person impeached Prince Qing Yikuang for pervasive bribery, requesting a monthly stipend of thirty thousand taels of silver to preserve his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he came to court and impeached Prince Qing Yikuang to his face for pervasive bribery, asking that he be given a monthly stipend of thirty thousand taels of silver to preserve his integrity.

sentences.zh: 又劾直隸總督袁世凱「權謀邁眾，城府阻深，能諂人又能用人，自得奕劻之助，其權威遂為我朝二百年來滿、漢疆臣所未有，引用私黨，佈滿要津。

translations.literal: He also impeached Zhili Governor-General Yuan Shikai: "His schemes surpass the multitude, his mind is deep and obstructive; he can flatter men and also employ men; since gaining Yikuang's help, his authority has become what no Manchu or Han frontier minister in our dynasty's two hundred years has possessed; he fills key posts with his private faction.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Zhili Governor-General Yuan Shikai: "His schemes surpass all others, his mind is deep and obstructive; he knows how to flatter and how to use men; with Yikuang's backing his authority exceeds anything a Manchu or Han frontier minister has held in our dynasty's two hundred years, and he fills key posts with his private faction.

sentences.zh: 我皇太后、皇上或未盡知，臣但有一日之官，即盡一日之心。

translations.literal: Our empress dowager and emperor may not fully know; as long as this subject holds office for a day, he will give his heart for a day.
translations.idiomatic: Our empress dowager and emperor may not fully know; yet as long as I hold office for a day, I will give my whole heart for that day.

sentences.zh: 言盡有淚，淚盡有血。

translations.literal: When words were exhausted there were tears; when tears were exhausted there was blood.
translations.idiomatic: When his words ran out, there were tears; when his tears ran out, there was blood.

sentences.zh: 奕劻、世凱若仍不悛，臣當隨時奏劾，以報天恩」。

translations.literal: If Yikuang and Shikai still do not repent, this subject will memorialize impeachment at any time, to repay heaven's grace."
translations.idiomatic: If Yikuang and Shikai still do not repent, I shall memorialize impeachment whenever the occasion arises, to repay heaven's grace."

sentences.zh: 詔訶責，引疾乞退。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him; he cited illness and begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him; he cited illness and begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 兩宮升遐，奔赴哭臨，越日即行，時之洞在樞垣，不一往謁也。

translations.literal: When the two empress dowagers passed away, he rushed to attend mourning rites and departed the next day; at the time Zhidong was in the Grand Council, yet he did not once go to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor passed away, he rushed to attend the mourning rites and left the next day; Zhidong was then in the Grand Council, yet Dingfen did not once go to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 明年，聞之洞喪，親送葬南皮。

translations.literal: The next year, hearing of Zhidong's death, he personally escorted the funeral to Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on hearing of Zhidong's death, he personally escorted the funeral to Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 及武昌事起，再入都，用直隸總督陳夔龍薦，以三品京堂候補。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang affair broke out, he entered the capital again; on Zhili Governor Chen Kuilong's recommendation he was made a third-rank Beijing official awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuchang affair broke out, he entered the capital again; on Zhili Governor Chen Kuilong's recommendation he was made a third-rank Beijing official awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 旋奉廣東宣慰使之命，粵中已大亂，道梗不得達，遂病嘔血。

translations.literal: Soon he received appointment as Guangdong pacification commissioner; Guangdong was already in great disorder, the roads blocked and he could not reach it, and he fell ill vomiting blood.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received appointment as Guangdong pacification commissioner; Guangdong was already in great disorder, the roads were blocked and he could not reach it, and he fell ill vomiting blood.

sentences.zh: 兩至梁格莊叩謁景皇帝暫安之殿，露宿寢殿旁，瞻仰流涕。

translations.literal: Twice he went to Lianggezhuang to kowtow and pay respects at the hall where the Guangxu Emperor temporarily resided, sleeping in the open beside the sleeping hall, gazing up in tears.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he went to Lianggezhuang to kowtow before the hall where the Guangxu Emperor temporarily resided, sleeping in the open beside the sleeping hall and gazing up in tears.

sentences.zh: 及孝定景皇后升遐，奉安崇陵，恭送如禮，自原留守陵寢，遂命管理崇陵種樹事。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xiaoding Jing passed away and was interred at Chongling, he escorted her with full rites; having himself requested to remain and guard the mausoleum, he was ordered to manage tree-planting at Chongling.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xiaoding Jing passed away and was interred at Chongling, he escorted her with full rites; having asked to remain and guard the mausoleum, he was ordered to manage tree-planting at Chongling.

sentences.zh: 旋命在毓慶宮行走。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve at the Yuqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to serve at the Yuqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁巳復辟，已臥病，強起周旋。

translations.literal: At the 1917 restoration he was already bedridden, yet forced himself up to attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the 1917 restoration he was already bedridden, yet forced himself up to attend to affairs.

sentences.zh: 事變憂甚，逾年卒，諡文忠。

translations.literal: Deeply grieved by the turn of events, he died the following year, posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply grieved by the turn of events, he died the following year and was given the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 徐坊，字梧生，山東臨清州人，巡撫延旭子。

translations.literal: Xu Fang, courtesy name Wusheng, was a native of Linqing prefecture in Shandong, son of Governor Yan Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fang, whose courtesy name was Wusheng, came from Linqing prefecture in Shandong; he was the son of Governor Yan Xu.

sentences.zh: 少納貲為戶部主事。

translations.literal: In youth he purchased office with contributions and became a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he purchased office with contributions and became a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，法陷諒山，延旭逮問，下刑部獄。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu, when the French took Langshan, Yan Xu was arrested and questioned and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Guangxu, when the French took Langshan, Yan Xu was arrested and questioned and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 坊侍至京師，入則慰母，出則省延旭於獄，橐饘之事，皆自任之，布衣蔬食，言輒流涕。

translations.literal: Fang attended him to the capital; entering he comforted his mother, going out he visited Yan Xu in prison; matters of carrying provisions he undertook entirely himself, wearing coarse cloth and eating plain food, speaking always with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Fang followed him to the capital; at home he comforted his mother, abroad he visited Yan Xu in prison; he undertook all the work of carrying provisions himself, wore coarse cloth and ate plain food, and wept whenever he spoke.

sentences.zh: 延旭戍新疆，未出都卒，坊扶柩歸葬，徒行泥淖中，道路嘆為孝子。

translations.literal: Yan Xu was to be exiled to Xinjiang; before leaving the capital he died, and Fang carried the coffin home for burial, walking through mud and mire— travelers on the road sighed at him as a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xu was to be exiled to Xinjiang; before leaving the capital he died, and Fang carried the coffin home for burial, walking through mud and mire—travelers on the road marveled at him as a filial son.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，奔赴西安行在。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he rushed to the imperial retinue at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he rushed to the imperial retinue at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 明年，扈駕返，以尚書榮慶薦，超擢國子丞。

translations.literal: The next year, escorting the court's return, on Minister Rongqing's recommendation he was specially promoted to vice-director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, escorting the court on its return, he was specially promoted to vice-director of the Directorate of Education on Minister Rongqing's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 鄂變起，連上五封事，俱不報。

translations.literal: When the Hubei uprising broke out, he submitted five sealed memorials in succession; none received response.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hubei uprising broke out, he submitted five sealed memorials in succession; none received a response.

sentences.zh: 遜位詔下，遂棄官。

translations.literal: When the abdication edict was issued, he abandoned office.
translations.idiomatic: When the abdication edict was issued, he resigned his office.

sentences.zh: 旋命行走毓慶宮，坊已久病，力疾入直。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve at the Yuqing Palace; Fang had long been ill, yet forced himself through illness to take up duty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to serve at the Yuqing Palace; Fang had long been ill, yet forced himself through illness to take up duty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，諡忠勤。

translations.literal: Before long he died, posthumous name Zhongqin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died and was given the posthumous name Zhongqin.

sentences.zh: 勞乃宣，字玉初，浙江桐鄉人。

translations.literal: Lao Naixuan, courtesy name Yuchu, was a native of Tongxiang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Naixuan, whose courtesy name was Yuchu, came from Tongxiang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治十年進士，以知縣分直隸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he passed as jinshi and was assigned as magistrate in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as a magistrate in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 查淶水禮王府圈地，力請減租蘇民困。

translations.literal: Investigating enclosed estates of the Liwang Mansion in Laishui, he strenuously requested rent reduction to relieve the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating enclosed estates of the Liwang Mansion in Laishui, he strenuously petitioned for rent reduction to relieve the people's hardship.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，初任臨榆，日晨起坐堂皇治官書，啟重門，民有呼籥者，立親訊之，使閽者不能隔吏役，吏役不能隔人民。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, on first taking office at Linyu, each morning he sat in the hall to handle official documents; opening the heavy gates, when the people called for justice he immediately examined the case in person, so that gatekeepers could not block clerks and runners, nor could clerks and runners block the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Guangxu, on first taking office at Linyu, each morning he sat in the hall to handle official business; when the heavy gates were opened and the people called for justice, he examined cases in person, so gatekeepers could not keep clerks and runners away, nor could clerks and runners keep the people away.

sentences.zh: 其後居官二十餘年皆如之。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years afterward in office he always did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years in office afterward, he always did the same.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃督師山海關，檄司文案。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guoquan commanded troops at Shanhaiguan, he was ordered to manage documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guoquan commanded troops at Shanhaiguan, he was ordered to manage documents in his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 歷南皮等縣，畿輔州縣遇道差，咸科於民有定額，而官取其贏。

translations.literal: Serving in Nanpi and other counties, in metropolitan prefectures and counties when relay couriers passed through, levies on the people had fixed quotas while officials took the surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Nanpi and other counties, he found that in metropolitan prefectures and counties relay expenses were levied on the people at fixed quotas while officials kept the surplus.

sentences.zh: 乃宣任蠡縣，值謁陵事竣，贏支應錢千餘緡，儲庫備公用。

translations.literal: When Naixuan served in Li county, after the tomb-visitation duties ended the surplus disbursement amounted to more than a thousand strings of cash, which he stored in the treasury for public use.
translations.idiomatic: When Naixuan served in Li county, after the tomb-visitation duties ended the surplus disbursement came to more than a thousand strings of cash, which he stored in the treasury for public use.

sentences.zh: 任完縣，購書萬餘卷庋尊經閣。

translations.literal: Serving in Wan county, he purchased more than ten thousand volumes of books and stored them in the Zunjing Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Wan county, he purchased more than ten thousand volumes of books and housed them in the Zunjing Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 任吳橋，創裡塾，農事畢，令民入塾，授以弟子規、小學內篇、聖諭廣訓諸書，歲盡始罷。

translations.literal: Serving in Wuqiao, he founded village schools; when farm work was finished he ordered the people to enter the schools and be taught the Rules for Students, the Inner Chapters of the Elementary Learning, the Amplified Instructions of the Sacred Edict, and other books, continuing until the year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Wuqiao, he founded village schools; when the farm work was done he had the people enter the schools and study the Rules for Students, the Inner Chapters of the Elementary Learning, the Amplified Instructions of the Sacred Edict, and other books, continuing until the year's end.

sentences.zh: 先是寧津奸民陳二糾黨為州郡害，土人稱曰黑團，勢甚熾。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Ningjin a wicked man named Chen Er gathered a faction to harm the prefecture and counties; locals called them the Black Gang, and their power was very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Ningjin a wicked man named Chen Er had gathered a faction that preyed on the prefecture and counties; locals called them the Black Gang, and their power ran very high.

sentences.zh: 嘗至南皮劫殺，乃宣會防營掩捕，擒陳二及其黨數人磔於市，黑團遂絕。

translations.literal: They once came to Nanpi to rob and kill; Naixuan joined with the defense camp in a surprise arrest, captured Chen Er and several of his followers, and dismembered them in the market—the Black Gang then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They once came to Nanpi to rob and kill; Naixuan joined the defense camp in a surprise arrest, captured Chen Er and several of his followers, and had them dismembered in the market—the Black Gang was then extinguished.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，義和拳起山東，蔓延於直、東各境，乃宣為義和拳教門源流考，張示曉諭，且申請奏頒禁止，不能行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Boxers arose in Shandong and spread through Zhili and the eastern provinces; Naixuan wrote An Inquiry into the Origins of the Boxer Sect, posted it for public notice and instruction, and also memorialized requesting an imperial prohibition—it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Boxers arose in Shandong and spread through Zhili and the eastern provinces; Naixuan wrote An Inquiry into the Origins of the Boxer Sect, posted it for public notice, and memorialized asking that an imperial prohibition be issued—it could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 景州有節小廷者，匪首也，號能降神。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou there was one Jie Xiaoting, a bandit chief who was said to be able to descend spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzhou there was a bandit chief named Jie Xiaoting, reputed to be able to descend spirits.

sentences.zh: 乃宣飭役捕治，縱士民環觀，既受笞，號呼不能作神狀，梟示之，匪乃不敢入境。

translations.literal: Naixuan ordered runners to arrest and punish him, allowing scholars and common people to surround and watch; after receiving the bastinado he cried out and could no longer play at being possessed by spirits; he was displayed by decapitation, and the bandits then dared not enter the district.
translations.idiomatic: Naixuan ordered runners to arrest and punish him, letting scholars and common people surround and watch; after the bastinado he cried out and could no longer play at spirit possession; he was decapitated and displayed, and the bandits then dared not enter the district.

sentences.zh: 明年，拳黨入京，乃宣知大亂將作，適調吏部稽勳司主事，遂請急南歸，浙撫任道鎔延主浙江大學堂。

translations.literal: The next year the Boxer faction entered the capital; Naixuan knew great disorder was about to break out; just then he was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's Records of Honors Office, and he requested urgent leave to return south; Zhejiang Governor Ren Daorong engaged him to head the Zhejiang Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Boxer faction entered the capital; Naixuan knew great disorder was imminent; just then he was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's Records of Honors Office, and he requested urgent leave to return south; Zhejiang Governor Ren Daorong engaged him to head the Zhejiang Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋入江督李興銳幕，端方、周馥繼任，咸禮重之。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the secretariat of Jiang Governor Li Xingrui; Duanfang and Zhou Fu succeeded in turn, and all honored him highly.
